To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the satellite based evaporation products are not consistent with the GRACE based water storage changes, in terms of both the temporal and spatial patterns of the retrieved variables.
the water budget closure is possible only when using a combination of remote sensing and in situ data.

(1) the evaporation estimates are not hydrologically consistent with the GRACE derived water balance, (2) there is no significant correlation between the GRACE derived terrestrial storage changes and the remote sensing based evapotranspiration estimates, and (3) the correlation between precipitation and evaporation estimates is weak and not significant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the hydrological consistency and water balance closure in dryland regions using remote sensing products and the GRACE derived terrestrial water storage changes.

the following: (a) the evaluation of the consistency between GRACE based water storage change and satellite evaporation estimates, and the comparison of satellite evaporation products with ground based measurements, and (b) the evaluation of GRACE derived water balance closure in two dryland basins, using satellite precipitation and evaporation products.

the following issues: (i) the hydrological consistency among remote sensing based products in terms of the closure of the water balance, (ii) the correlation between the spatial patterns of evaporation (E), precipitation (P) and terrestrial water storages changes (P E) as derived from satellite observations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the water balance closure is not possible using satellite data alone in these dryland regions.
the GRACE data is not suitable for water balance closure in dryland regions.
remote sensing data can be used to monitor evaporation and precipitation in the dryland regions but the water budget closure is not possible with the current data sets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
satellite data are not yet able to close the regional water balance.
the water balance cannot be closed with the satellite data alone.
the evaporation estimates are not consistent with each other, nor with the GRACE derived water budget.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the spatial correlation of P and E, as well as of E and GRACE derived water storages is not high, and that the correlation of E with P and with GRACE water storage is higher when E is estimated using remote sensing data with a higher spatial resolution.
the water storage changes derived from GRACE are not consistent with the water budget closure using the satellite based estimates of evapotranspiration and precipitation.
, in order to improve the consistency of satellite derived evaporation estimates, the evaporation component should be modeled separately from the precipitation and water storage changes.
